title: billing.invoice.created payload
description: THE BREAKAGE. billing reserved `invoice_id` in its manifest and this contract publishes it again — the same service, the same surface, the name both reserved and live. Nothing errors: the schema is valid, the manifest is valid, the payload still round-trips. What a consumer gets is a generated struct whose `InvoiceId` field now means whatever this document says, under a name it already trusted. That is `reserved.reintroduced`, and it is a FAILURE rather than a warning because the reader who would have noticed is a downstream consumer who will not report it as a schema problem.

invoice_id.description: Put BACK, six months after being removed and reserved. This is the whole hazard in one property: the name a consumer's generated source still carries, pointing at a field whose meaning nobody renegotiated.
